approvalWasConditionalOnOneThing.condition: the executable support code had to be brought into exact agreement with the already-approved R3 semantics
approvalWasConditionalOnOneThing.defect: R3 freezes an AMBIGUOUS attempt as BLOCKED - neither counted against the budget nor released for retry - but attemptConsumption.ts expressed only the first half. DevConfirmBudget and FinalHoldoutState returned BLOCKED, incremented nothing, and then accepted a further attempt, which releases the candidate for retry BY OMISSION. discloseAttempt() would also have accepted BLOCKED paired with a terminal outcome.
approvalWasConditionalOnOneThing.theMethodologyWasNotAtFault: The defect was in the support module's state machine, never in the R3 text. No methodology byte was changed to fix it.

boundDecisions.d7Detail: Prompt-development disclosure gains exactly two procedural tokens and nothing item-level: the terminal outcome token ACCEPT / REJECT / INADMISSIBLE, and the attempt consumption state CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED.

boundAttemptConsumptionRule.boundaryType: MONOTONIC - once TRUE it can never return to FALSE
boundAttemptConsumptionRule.boundaryIsNotANewInvention: It is the Methodology V2 name for the already-frozen F0V predeclared inclusion rule, CLASS C (PROVIDER_REQUEST_OR_SEMANTIC_EXECUTION_OBSERVED), implemented in src/test/harness/phase2b2d2c/f0w/sequencing.ts.
boundAttemptConsumptionRule.aPreRequestRecordIsNecessaryButNotSuffic: An orgunit_classifier_calls row, or a passing child preflight, records an INTENT to dispatch, not a dispatch. The boundary is set by POSITIVE evidence of execution, never by the absence of a refusal record. On 2026-09-16 the opposite reading spent all ten F0X candidate slots on ten children that had issued zero provider requests.

devConfirmBudget.preSemanticInadmissible: NOT_CONSUMED; the byte-identical candidate may retry once the pre-semantic defect is repaired
devConfirmBudget.postSemanticInadmissible: CONSUMED; it costs a slot exactly as an ACCEPT or a REJECT does
devConfirmBudget.candidateDeterminedRealisedDenominatorFa: POST-SEMANTIC by definition and ALWAYS consumes - the G3 unit-page precision case - so precision cannot be dodged by predicting UNIT_PAGE almost never

whatStickyMeans: DEV_CONFIRM: while a block is unresolved, no next candidate and no retry of the same candidate may begin; consumedAttemptCount does not increment; the methodology generation stays halted
FINAL_HOLDOUT: a blocked holdout is neither AVAILABLE nor RETIRED, and no semantic attempt of any kind may be recorded against it
only an explicit owner adjudication clears a block, it is one-shot, and BLOCKED is not an admissible adjudication result
adjudicate CONSUMED: clear the block, increment exactly once (retire the FINAL_HOLDOUT irreversibly), close the generation if that is the third consumed attempt
adjudicate NOT_CONSUMED: clear the block, increment nothing, and restore only the existing byte-identical + repaired-pre-semantic-defect retry right
an unresolvable adjudication resolves to CONSUMED; NOT_CONSUMED requires the frozen NOT_STARTED condition to be POSITIVELY established, never merely the absence of positive request evidence
ambiguousBlockedSemantics.aBlockedAttemptIsNotTerminal: It has no terminal outcome and no settled consumption, so it has no terminal disclosure. discloseAttempt() refuses BLOCKED rather than fabricating INADMISSIBLE + BLOCKED, and blocked owner/audit state travels a separate surface carrying no item id, organisation, coarse reason or realised denominator.

boundAttemptConsumptionRule.theR3TextWasNotChangedToMatchTheCode: The support build was changed to match the already-approved text. The R3 bytes describe these semantics exactly as approved; the module's own capability summary inside the R3 bytes names the eight exports that existed when R3 was written, and the adjudication members the support build adds are a strictly additive enforcement of sectionO_attemptConsumption.ambiguousAttempts, not a new rule.

boundHoldoutDisposition.aFinalHoldoutMustBeFreshlyDrawn: Any FINAL_HOLDOUT under Methodology V2 is drawn from a corpus that does not yet exist. This approval creates none.
